Research on whether brain training improves cognitive function shows conflicting outcomes. Some studies, particularly those involving structured research settings like the ACTIVE trial, report improved mental skills in trained areas with benefits lasting years [d1]. Other sources suggest that engaging in novel, challenging real-world activities such as learning an instrument or physical exercise can support cognitive health [d4, d5, d8]. However, multiple rigorous studies and consensus statements find that commercial computerized brain-training programs lack evidence for improving general cognitive function or transferring benefits to everyday life [d3, d6, d9, d10, d11]. Thus, the scientific community remains divided, with evidence supporting specific, research-based interventions but not broadly endorsing commercial brain games.
